    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 23,879 on Thursday, Nov.
    • The standard line for a bear market is a 20% fall from the high.
    • I'm not predicting the index gets there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) finished at 23,879 on Thursday, Nov. 19. The tech-heavy index now sits about 13.5% below its Oct. 6 record close of 27,600 -- a correction, though not a bear market.

    The standard line for a bear market is a 20% fall from the high. For the Nasdaq, that's a close near 22,080, or about another 7.5% drop from Thursday's level.

    I'm not predicting the index gets there. But a plan is easier to stick to when it's written down before a sell-off than during one, and mine is this: If the Nasdaq closes in bear-market territory, the first stock I'll buy is Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%)(GOOG -2.59%).

    Shares of the Google parent closed at $272.66 on Thursday, their lowest close since October 2025. The stock's now about 32% below where it finished the day on May 13, at a record close of $402.62 -- more than double the Nasdaq's decline from its own high.

    It has been revealed that A lot of that drop came in a single session. The stock fell about 13% on Oct. 29, the day after Alphabet posted third-quarter results showing slower Search growth, lower earnings per share, and a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow.

    In other words, the stock's arguably already taken the sort of hit a bear market brings, while the business underneath keeps growing.

    It has been revealed that showing how well the business has held up through the drop, Alphabet's revenue growth has accelerated all year. Sales grew 22% year over year in the first quarter, then 24% in the second, and third-quarter sales rose 25% to $127.6 billion. Operating income grew 30% year over year in all three quarters. And in the first nine months of 2026, operating income came to $121 billion, a 30% jump from $93 billion a year before.

    In a recent development, I focus on operating income because Alphabet's net income swings with the value of its stakes in other companies. Other income (mainly investment gains) added around $127 billion in the same nine months.

    According to recent reports, that noted, not every number is heading the right way. Last year's third quarter had a $3.5 billion European Commission fine, so without it, operating income rose more like 17% in the latest quarter. And as spending on artificial intelligence (AI) demonstrates up in costs, the operating margin has shrunk. It was 31.8% in the third quarter, versus 34% in the April-to-June period and 36.1% in the first quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that the second reason is the balance sheet. Alphabet expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, and management noted that amount is expected to rise significantly in 2027. A bear market could make raising money for that sort of spending more expensive.

    Industry observers note that but Alphabet has already raised a lot of it. In the first nine months of 2026, the company raised about $85 billion in upcoming debt, about $43 billion by selling common stock, and another $19 billion by issuing preferred stock.

    Alphabet's cash and marketable securities totaled $265.1 billion at the end of September, more than twice its total at the end of 2025. Long-term debt was $125.1 billion.

    Sources indicate that yes, selling new shares dilutes current shareholders, and free cash flow was negative in both of the past two quarters. But with around $140 billion more in cash and marketable securities than in long-term debt, Alphabet arguably doesn't need a steady stock market to keep funding its build-out.

    Alphabet stock doesn't look expensive to me now. At $272.66, it costs around 18 times expected 2027 earnings, while Meta Platforms, another ad-driven tech giant, trades at about 17 times its expected 2027 earnings. For a business growing operating income by double digits, I think the price is fair.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that I wouldn't argue with anyone buying some now. The reason to wait for the line is that a bear market would probably mark down many stocks at once. Deciding beforehand which one gets the first dollar stops me from chasing whatever happened to fall the most that week.

    Alphabet doesn't have to track the index, either. But if it just matched the Nasdaq's remaining 7.5% drop from Thursday's close, the stock would trade near $252, or about 17 times expected 2027 earnings.

    If the Nasdaq closes 20% below its record, Alphabet is likely where my strategy begins.

    Industry observers note that sure, the index might never get there. And if it doesn't, Alphabet at around 18 times expected 2027 earnings still looks fairly priced to me.

In Q3 2026, he was busy scooping up several artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%), Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%), and Meta Platforms (META -5.93%).

    Let's look at what may have attracted Loeb to these names.

    Loeb's buy of Nvidia shares came before CEO Jensen Huang stepped down, but the tech giant remains in the pole position in the AI infrastructure build-out. Nvidia today is more than just a graphics processing unit (GPU) provider, offering a complete AI factory solution that includes networking, central processing units (CPUs), language processing units (LPUs) for the decode phase of inference, its Nemotron open-weight models, and an expanding software layer.

    That package has helped Nvidia increase its revenue per gigawatt from around $18 billion when it introduced its Hopper architecture a few years ago to around $40 billion today with Vera Rubin.

    With future memory and manufacturing capacity locked in, along with its strong ecosystem, expect Nvidia to remain the AI infrastructure leader over the coming years.

    SpaceX is one of the most exciting companies on the planet as it looks to disrupt industries and conquer space. The tech giant recently achieved a major milestone by catching the upper stage of its Starship rocket, setting it up to fundamentally change the economics of space introduces as it moves toward rapid reuse. This is also a stepping stone for SpaceX to hit some of its loftier goals, such as orbital data centers, Earth-to-Earth transport, and asteroid mining.

    Back on Earth, SpaceX has become one of the world's largest neocloud companies and plans to rapidly grow its AI infrastructure-as-a-service business. Right now, it is getting great rates on its AI infrastructure through short-term rentals, allowing it to see a payback on its investments within a year. The firm also plans to disrupt the U.S. mobile market, and its Cursor AI coding platform is growing quickly.

    It has been revealed that microsoft continues to see strong growth in both its Azure cloud computing unit and its enterprise software business. Azure has been a persistent 30%-plus revenue grower, with its revenue growth hitting 48% last quarter. With significant commitments from OpenAI and an overall $677 billion backlog, Azure should remain a strong growth driver in the years ahead.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, the organization has been gaining significant traction with its AI Copilot assistants across Microsoft 365 and its GitHub code repository. The shift to a seat-plus-consumption model has been paying off, and Copilot usage has been surging, with it seeing an eightfold year-over-year increase in seats last quarter. Given how embedded the company's software and governance tools are in the enterprise space, it looks well positioned to emerge as an AI software-as-a-service (SaaS) winner.

    Meta Platforms has been one of the best companies at using AI to drive growth in an already established, strong business. It's employing AI to both keep owners on its apps longer by displaying more content they are interested in and to feed them more relevant ads. This is leading to higher ad loads, stronger conversions, and better ad pricing.

    Last quarter, its revenue surged 26%, with a 14% increase in average price per ad and a 10% jump in ad impressions.

    Perhaps more exciting, though, is that Meta is jumping headfirst into consumer AI agents. These agents can help users with a multitude of tasks, but Meta will benefit most when they make purchases on a user's behalf. Here, Meta will get a cut of the transaction fee, giving it another potential new large revenue stream and putting it at the forefront of agentic commerce.

    After Its Worst Week in 18 Years, Nvidia Now Faces an SEC Investigation. What It Means for Investors

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you think you've had a bad week, just be glad you're not on Nvidia's (NVDA -14.01%) management team.
    • Shares of the top AI stock fell 23% this week, wiping out roughly $1 trillion from its market cap.
    • Reuters mentioned that the SEC was investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, but did not provide many details beyond that.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:10AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    If you think you've had a bad week, just be glad you're not on Nvidia's (NVDA -14.01%) management team.

    Shares of the top AI stock fell 23% this week, wiping out roughly $1 trillion from its market cap. It was its worst weekly performance since October 2008 during the height of the financial crisis. The slide was initially sparked by Jensen Huang's resignation the week before, and even a strong earnings report on Tuesday wasn't enough to stem the sell-off. On Friday, Nvidia stock plunged 14%, heading sharply lower in the afternoon after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission had opened an investigation into the manufacturer over accounting irregularities. That comes in addition to multiple investigations from different agencies and branches of the federal government over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese agent and possible violation of chip export rules.

    Reuters mentioned that the SEC was investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, but did not provide many details beyond that. Its report came three days after The Wall Street Journal said the SEC was investigating Nvidia, but did not say what for.

    Given the other news last week and the Commerce Dept. issuing tighter chip export rules to Southeast Asia, the SEC probe could focus on how Nvidia reports geographic revenue, which potentially obfuscates where its chips end up. Last year, it changed how it records geographic revenue, shifting it from billing addresses to customer headquarters. As a result of that change, the manufacturer no longer reports revenue from Singapore as its own line item.

    In fiscal 2026, Nvidia recorded $19.7 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, likely from permitted chips, though the SEC may be curious about how chips that ended up in China via other countries were recorded.

    It's important for investors to understand that an investigation doesn't mean that Nvidia committed fraud, or that it will face any enforcement actions.

    A probe is not evidence of wrongdoing, and many are closed without going further.

    Given the other news surrounding Nvidia, the SEC probe seems less surprising and may not be as impactful on the stock as it otherwise would be, as the manufacturer is already in turmoil. Even a finding of wrongdoing wouldn't be a terminal event for Nvidia, though it could damage its reputation, in addition to any fines or consequences the company could face.

    Executives at Super Micro Computer, a server-maker and close partner of Nvidia, were charged by the DOJ with conspiring to divert AI servers to China, though Supermicro's internal investigation found that no one on the senior management team was aware of the diversion scheme.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It will take months or longer for the investigations into Nvidia to play out, and the firm is likely to continue to receive scrutiny from the media in the wake of Huang's departure and the myriad investigations now surrounding it.

    Investors will note that Nvidia's forward P/E has fallen all the way to 8 as the stock has plunged, but with so much uncertainty surrounding the stock, buying it seems speculative at this point, and the stock's future performance depends on what the investigations uncover.

    Nvidia's "circular financing" is also in the spotlight after the change in leadership, and that could get attention from the SEC as well.

    According to recent reports, there's simply so much we don't know about the stock and its future right now. Risk-tolerant investors may choose to buy the stock at the current price, but they should be aware that the volatility for Nvidia, after it's fallen for seven sessions in a row, is likely to continue.

    By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:39AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Target ›.

    Value stocks have dominated growth stocks over the past year, an about-face from the previous three years of this market.

    The Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV -1.62%) is up 17% over the past 12 months, while its large-cap counterpart, the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) is up just 1%.

    And Vanguard strategists are not alone in thinking that value stocks will outperform growth stocks over the next 10 years, due to several factors, including overvalued large-cap growth stocks and the broadening out of AI, among other reasons.

    If you are looking for value stocks to set and forget for the next five years, consider these three.

    Industry observers note that target (TGT -0.97%) has had a resurgence over the past year or so after years of underperformance. The significant-box retail stock has returned a staggering 71% year to date and 89% over the past year. At the same time, it is still pretty cheap, trading at 18 times forward earnings after being beaten down for several years.

    It has been revealed that the turnaround has been fueled by its new CEO, Michael Fiddelke, who has boosted revenue and traffic through a combination of price cuts, increased digital sales, improved customer experience and inventory management, increased membership, and digital advertising through its Roundel business. He has been able to increase the gross margin, despite cutting prices, by streamlining and leaning into higher-margin growth areas.

    Target also benefited from a low valuation and favorable year-over-year comps.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The comps won't be as favorable next year, and the valuation won’t be as low, but Target has been able to reset to better compete with Walmart (WMT +1.51%) and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) while leaning into its strengths and not trying to be everything to everyone.

    It also has one of the best, most reliable dividends, which it has increased for 54 straight years.

    Dollar General (DG -2.23%) is another retail stock that has embarked on a turnaround plan.

    It has been revealed that it introduced two store-remodeling prepares in recent years: Project Renovate and Project Elevate. The plan is to overhaul or update some 4,250 stores this year, and those projects are expected to be complete by the end of fiscal 2026.

    Dollar General has poured some $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion in capital expenditures into these and other projects this year, and about $1.2 billion in 2025.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But it is already starting to reap the benefits. In the second quarter, net sales rose 5.2%, same-store sales increased 3.5%, operating profit rose 29%, and earnings jumped 33% to $2.48 per share. When all remodels are finished, Dollar General anticipates a 6% sales boost from fully remodeled stores and a 3% increase from upgraded stores.

    Along with these renovations, Dollar General has taken steps to improve inventory management and focus on higher-margin sales items by eliminating much of the inventory that either wasn't selling or had lower margins.

    According to recent reports, it positions Dollar General to defend its stake as the premier deep-discount retailer. The stock is pretty cheap with a P/E ratio of 17, a forward P/E of 16, and a five-year PEG ratio of 0.41, which indicates that it is a long-term value relative to its earnings expectations.

    In a recent development, micron (MU -13.89%) is one of the most explosive growth stocks on the market, yet it is trading in value territory, so it is basically a value stock. Shares are up 141% year to date and 200% over the past 12 months as the high bandwidth memory AI chipmaker is one of three major players in its booming industry.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that micron is at the center of a memory and storage supercycle in which the supply of memory chips for AI computing cannot keep up with demand. This has given Micron incredible pricing power and a massive backlog with more than 75% of the manufacturer's fiscal 2027 shipments already under contract. It is already booking out into fiscal 2028. Chief Operating Officer Manish Bhatia stated on the Q4 earnings call that Micron is seeing "stronger demand drivers than we've seen before" for 2027 and 2028.

    It also has long-term strategic customer agreements with 26 customers that will account for more than 35% of the capacity Micron will supply through 2030 — and those agreements are likely to continue to increase over time.

    The expected growth is outpacing price projections, as Micron stock is trading at just 10 times earnings and 4 times forward earnings. Further, it has a PEG ratio of just 0.15. It is the best value of these three stocks right now.

    All three of these stocks are cheap, with growth catalysts that should make them stocks to buy and hold for the next several years.

    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

    In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy tech giant with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

    Recent findings suggest that recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the firm delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    Recent findings suggest that tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the firm "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

    In a recent development, about the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," said Tonet.

    Recent findings suggest that tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that this week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    The 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the firm's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

    "We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," mentioned Mehta.

    In a recent development, the analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the tech giant's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

    Mehta ranks No. 401 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.8%. See Permian Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding manufacturer. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

    Recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

    Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

    Sources indicate that furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex plan to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

    "We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," stated Smith.

    Latest Update: Should You Forget SpaceX Stock?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (429 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • Sources indicate that wall Street appears to love Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) stock.
    • In fact, I think there's a compelling case that investors should forget about SpaceX stock entirely -- at least for a few years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Sources indicate that wall Street appears to love Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) stock. The current consensus price target is around $267, suggesting 93% upside potential.

    I'm not nearly as optimistic. In fact, I think there's a compelling case that investors should forget about SpaceX stock entirely -- at least for a few years.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    I love SpaceX as a business. I'm just not so sure about the stock.

    My biggest concern is simply a matter of timing. To justify its $1.9 trillion valuation, SpaceX will ultimately need to source hundreds of billions in fresh capital, successfully commercialize its Starship rocket, significantly scale both terrestrial and orbital data center infrastructure, and likely begin producing its own AI chips.

    It has been revealed that all this will take years to fully realize. Yet today's valuation largely assumes much of this will occur as promised.

    Sources indicate that to be clear, I'm not necessarily a SpaceX bear. In fact, I believe the manufacturer will play a key role in the AI economy. But its growth trajectory is full of execution risk, and it wouldn't be a surprise to see the company's growth roadmap take years longer than expected.

    When sizable growth is already priced in -- SpaceX right now trades above 50 times sales while reporting negative profits and cash flow -- small shifts in sentiment can have a large impact on the stock price, especially if discounted cash flows are being counted on far into the future.

    There are two likely paths forward for SpaceX. The first is that the company executes its growth proposal as expected, but returns to shareholders are blunted, given that much of that growth is already priced in. The second is that the company's growth journey doesn't go exactly as planned, leading to potential buying opportunities over the next few years.

    I'm betting on the latter. So while I'll keep an eye on the stock's valuation, I'm largely forgetting about it as a near-term investment opportunity.

    Chipotle Mexican Grill vs. e.l.f. Beauty: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:27AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Chipotle Mexican Grill ›.
    • Investors seeking resilient growth among consumer stocks often weigh the merits of dominant restaurant leaders against rising retail disruptors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:27AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Chipotle Mexican Grill ›.

    Investors seeking resilient growth among consumer stocks often weigh the merits of dominant restaurant leaders against rising retail disruptors. Choosing between Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG -2.07%) and e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) requires understanding how each manages scale and profitability.

    Chipotle relies on its massive physical footprint and premium brand perception to drive consistent returns. Meanwhile, e.l.f. Beauty uses a lean manufacturing model and digital prowess to gain market share from established legacy brands. This comparison explores which business model offers the most compelling path forward.

    It has been revealed that chipotle operates over 4,000 company-owned restaurants across North America and Europe, focusing on a limited menu of burritos and bowls made from fresh ingredients. The business strategy centers on high-volume throughput, particularly through its Chipotlane drive-thru format, which enhances convenience for digital orders. While the company owns its locations, it relies heavily on third-party delivery services, which accounted for roughly 16% of food and beverage revenue in the latest reporting year.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $12.7 billion, representing a growth rate of 7.9% compared to the prior period. The company remains highly profitable, generating net income of $1.4 billion during those twelve months. This performance reflects a steady net margin of 10.8%, as the company successfully balanced higher ingredient costs with incremental menu price increases to maintain its bottom line.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio stood at 1.2x, which measures the ability to cover short-term obligations with assets that can be converted to cash within a year. The debt-to-equity ratio was 1.8x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity to measure financial leverage. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $1.4 billion, providing ample capital for the tech giant to continue expanding its restaurant count without seeking external financing.

    e.l.f. Beauty is a multi-brand powerhouse in the beauty and retail stocks space, offering clean and vegan cosmetics at price points significantly lower than prestige competitors. The company sells its products through major retail partners including Target (TGT -0.97%), Walmart (WMT +1.51%), and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). By maintaining a rapid innovation cycle, the company can bring trending beauty products to market much faster than traditional industry giants.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $1.9 billion, a substantial increase of 39.9% over the previous year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by net income of $86.6 million, resulting in a net margin of about 4.5%. While the manufacturer has prioritized market share gains and brand acquisitions, it has remained consistently profitable during this period of high-velocity growth.

    Sources indicate that as of its March 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio was strong at 2.3x, indicating a robust liquidity position. The debt-to-equity ratio was 0.8x, suggesting the company maintains a conservative level of financial leverage. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow was $190.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 40.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Sources indicate that chipotle faces significant risks related to food safety and food-borne illnesses, which are exacerbated by its reliance on fresh produce and raw ingredients. It operates in a highly competitive restaurant industry, facing pressure from traditional chains like Starbucks (SBUX -1.28%), meal kits, and delivery aggregators. Additionally, labor shortages and the need to comply with complex employment laws, including fair workweek and just cause legislation, pose risks to operational consistency and cost management.

    e.l.f. Beauty faces intense competition in the beauty industry from major rivals such as Coty (COTY -2.47%), with a reliance on maintaining brand relevance and shelf space. The firm's heavy reliance on third-party manufacturers, particularly in China, exposes it to geopolitical risks, supply chain disruptions, and tariff volatility. Furthermore, the company faces risks related to integrating acquisitions, such as rhode and Naturium, and must navigate complex, evolving data privacy and AI regulations.

    e.l.f. Beauty trades at a lower earnings multiple than Chipotle, although both companies right now command similar valuations when measured against their trailing sales.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Chipotle and e.l.f. Beauty represent two very different consumer stocks. The former is an established player with higher margins while e.l.f. Beauty is a rising star, producing outsized sales growth. This makes choosing between them a tough decision. Ultimately, I would recommend Chipotle.

    The restaurant chain's robust net margin of 10.8% compared to e.l.f. Beauty's 4.5% is hard to ignore, as is its return on equity of 52.5% versus e.l.f. Beauty's 7.4% over the trailing 12 months. These factors contribute to its higher share price valuation.

    Industry observers note that moreover, Chipotle expects to end 2026 with 350 to 370 newly introduced restaurants with 80% of them including a Chipotlane, contributing to the firm's throughput. It forecasts 340 to 360 new restaurants in 2027, which provides a clear runway to revenue expansion next year.

    Recent findings suggest that e.l.f. Beauty is seeing spectacular sales growth. In its fiscal second quarter, ended Sept. 30, it posted an impressive 51% year-over-year increase to $520.8 million, representing the 31st consecutive quarter of net sales growth. However, its slimmer margins, heavy marketing spend, tough year-over-year comparisons, and supply-chain execution could weigh on earnings momentum, further tilting toward Chipotle as the better stock for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has been a rough stock to own over the past few weeks.
    • It has been revealed that in the meantime, I think there are several great companies available to invest in, with Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) being one of the best options.
    • In a recent development, nvidia's primary products are graphics processing units (GPUs), which are incredible computing units that can process multiple calculations in parallel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:31AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has been a rough stock to own over the past few weeks. It has lost its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, and some investors worry it may never recover. While the board searches for a new leader to fill his shoes, investors are waiting to see what happens next.

    It has been revealed that in the meantime, I think there are several great companies available to invest in, with Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) being one of the best options. Broadcom is a direct competitor of Nvidia and has some advantages over Nvidia. That could lead to it stealing more market share during the current turmoil, making it a top stock to consider buying now.

    In a recent development, nvidia's primary products are graphics processing units (GPUs), which are incredible computing units that can process multiple calculations in parallel. While these units are great at nearly any task, they don't specialize in any one task. Some of this potential is wasted when a GPU is used for one workload throughout its lifespan. A specific and purpose-built computing unit would do a better job in these scenarios, and that's where Broadcom steps in.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that broadcom has emerged as a great partner for designing custom AI chips, and many companies have already partnered with it and launched their own custom AI chips. However, there has been no larger partner than Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%). Alphabet and Broadcom collaborated to design and build its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which can outperform GPUs in many scenarios from a cost perspective. These units are fantastic, and companies like Anthropic have designed much of their computing infrastructure around them.

    It has been revealed that with Nvidia GPUs expensive and not purpose-built, many AI companies are turning to custom AI chips like the TPU to deliver the computing power they need at a lower price point. This is translating into huge growth for Broadcom, and it's growing even faster than Nvidia is.

    According to recent reports, broadcom hasn't been shy about telling investors of the impressive growth that's coming down the pipeline. During its most recent conference call, management revealed guidance that AI semiconductor revenue will double in 2027 to $115 billion. Furthermore, Broadcom revealed that that figure is expected to double again to $230 billion in 2028. It doesn't get much better than that, and investors are bound to be happy with returns if Broadcom can follow through on that projection.

    Industry observers note that despite that projection, Broadcom's stock isn't valued at all that high. Broadcom is already in fiscal year 2027, and trades at just 17 times next year's earnings.

    AVGO PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    That's a very cheap price tag to pay for a stalwart like Broadcom.

    Broadcom also doesn't carry the same risks as a firm like Nvidia, where a questionable portion of sales is being diverted to China. Broadcom's customers are well-known, and there isn't much risk of its products falling into the wrong hands. This is a key factor that many investors ignore, along with the fact that Broadcom's products are starting to steal data center market share.

    Recent findings suggest that I think all of this adds up to Broadcom being one of the best investment options right now. It's cheap, growing swiftly, doesn't have export risk, and has a stable leadership team. That is a recipe for success in the AI world, and I think Broadcom shareholders will be well rewarded over the long term.

    Now is a perfect time to buy amid the turmoil in the market surrounding AI stocks. By this time next year, Broadcom's stock will likely be much higher.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    According to recent reports, after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he noted.

    "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," noted DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    In a recent development, while Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as latest contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    Industry observers note that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

    In a recent development, the 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space firm with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Industry observers note that gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

    "Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," remarked Anmuth.

    In the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst noted. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst said. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

    While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

    It has been revealed that anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

    Industry News: Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud tech giant CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Industry observers note that chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    According to recent reports, chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    Recent findings suggest that after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security tech giant, Powell mentioned. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Industry observers note that powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    It has been revealed that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he mentioned. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," mentioned Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    In a recent development, devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    #50786. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1038 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, stated Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    It has been revealed that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    In a recent development, the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Sources indicate that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she noted.

    It has been revealed that "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she remarked.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    It has been revealed that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Sources indicate that it's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, remarked R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    Recent findings suggest that "That's when spreads really widen out," he stated. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
    • Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround blueprint.

    Recent findings suggest that following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," remarked Wright.

    The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    In a recent development, wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the organization's AI strategy when it unveils its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active people in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," stated the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently introduced Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the organization's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Industry observers note that morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, next is semiconductor organization Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    Sources indicate that the five-star analyst stated that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    In a recent development, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the manufacturer raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Svanberg stated that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

    📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    It has been revealed that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    According to recent reports, specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Industry observers note that furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in newly introduced wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    It has been revealed that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream tech giant operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Sources indicate that ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the organization to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," noted Mackay.

    Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production tech giant with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent revealed an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," mentioned Richardson.

    In a recent development, the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable tech giant, regardless of market conditions.

    Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    #50731. Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

    📅 27 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (345 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

    📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (345 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • In a recent development, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    In a recent development, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    It has been revealed that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    According to recent reports, robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the organization has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    In a recent development, net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.
